body:
**Canvas theme-level typography panel** · explored 2026-08-26

**The answer: A, with D folded into it. B later, C not now.**

Colours already live in the Theme tab of the right rail. Type belongs there too, as a new section, because that's where someone goes to change how the design *looks* rather than one node. **A** is that section.

**D is the part of A that is easy to get wrong.** A preset stores only the controls it authors; the rest inherit from `default`. A panel that writes all three values on first drag would quietly sever that link. D's filled/hollow dot is the fix.

**B is the demo, not the home.** The same controls floating over the board — worth building after A, but it competes with the canvas for space.

**C is A at dialog scale**, earned only when typography outgrows a 320px rail.

**First commit:** `set_typeset` is MCP-only today; it needs an HTTP route and client. While dragging, write the CSS variables directly and commit once on pointer-up.

**A — A Typography section in the Theme tab** · RECOMMENDED

A new accordion section in the Theme tab: typeset switcher, the three rhythm controls, the three face roles, and a resolved-ladder readout.

- **Fits what is there.** Same accordion and triggers; no new surface to discover.
- **The readout is free.** `get_theme` already returns the resolved type scale, so `h1 40 / 0.95` is real data — the honest answer to "what did that slider actually do".
- **Faces are roles, not stacks** (`sans`, `display`, `mono`), so they compose with `set_fonts`.
- **Failure mode.** 320px is tight once you show inherited-vs-authored per control (see D); the readout stays at four rungs.
- **Cost.** One section, one numeric slider control, plus the `set_typeset` route. Smallest path to all the acceptance criteria.

**D — Typeset manager: inheritance made visible** · FOLD INTO A

One card per typeset, each control marked authored here (filled dot) or inherited from `default` (hollow dot, muted value). The header shows the generated selector — `:root`, `.typeset-docs`.

- **It is the model, not a view of it.** `docs` stores only `{ leading, flow }`; its size follows `default` forever. Three sliders with no state distinction can't express that, and the first drag would destroy it.
- **Clearing is a real operation.** `set_typeset` accepts `null` to drop a field — the hollow dot as a verb.
- **Naming the selector teaches the feature** — the cheapest possible documentation.
- **Failure mode.** Standalone it's a list with no editing, which is why it's a layer on A's control rows, not its own tab.

**C — Typography workbench (dialog scope)** · NOT NOW

A full dialog in the shape of the settings dialog: typeset rail, controls column, and the complete ten-rung ladder beside a live specimen.

- **What only this can do.** Typography is the one theme axis where you judge the *relationship between sizes*, and a 320px rail shows one rung at a time.
- **The specimen is not a mock** — it's a `Prose` region governed by the same variables the sliders write.
- **Why not now.** Same controls and mutation as A in more space — a second surface for the same state. Build it when typography needs per-role overrides, a measure/contrast report, or side-by-side preset comparison.
- **If it is built**, it opens *from* A and shares its control components.
- **Cost.** Highest of the four, and none of it on the critical path.

**B — Floating rhythm HUD over the board** · AFTER A

The three controls in a bar docked over the canvas, so you drag while every frame re-flows underneath. The frames are real `Prose` regions at three typesets — `default`, `.typeset-docs`, `.typeset-compact`.

- **This is the demo.** "Drag one slider, watch six frames re-rhythm" only reads if the controls sit *over* the work, not 320px away in the rail.
- **Cheap once A exists** — a second rendering of the same binding, not a second implementation.
- **What it cannot be.** No room for face pickers, presets or a ladder, so a companion to A, never a replacement. It needs its own open/dismiss state and a way back.
- **Failure mode.** It occludes the board; opened by default it becomes chrome that gets closed once and never reopened.
